measure_line: Share of citizens 18 and over who reported voting, November 2024, the ten states with the most voting-age citizens, with each figure’s 90 percent margin of error
reading_guide: Each line spans a state’s margin of error, and a gap counts only past the gap’s own margin. A filled dot differs from the nation by more than the margin; an open dot sits within it.
notes_internal: Rule 14.9's correct plate on the kit's range-bar form (ED-E4). Checked by script: five states past the gap's margin from the nation (the form's labels.test reads the same margins), five within it; the ranked ends inside their own margins. Each state is part of the nation, so the exact test (the data lead's RF-7, ST S4) is the square root of a²(1 − 2w) + b², with w the state's share of the nation's citizens of voting age (3.2 to 10.7 percent here); the generator checks that it sets apart the same five states as the independent test the kit draws (California 1.68 falls to 1.50 against a gap of 0.6; Ohio 2.55 to 2.46 against 2.1).
reader_question: Which of the largest states differ from the nation in reported turnout, past the margin of error?
title: Five of the ten states with the most voting-age citizens differed from the nation’s 65.3 percent turnout by more than the margin of error.
notes: Past the margin: Michigan, Pennsylvania, Florida, New York and Texas. Within it: Ohio, Illinois, California, North Carolina and Georgia.
source_line: Source: U.S. Census Bureau, Current Population Survey Voting and Registration Supplement, Table 4a, reported voting for states, November 2024, 50 states and DC. Retrieved November 6, 2026. Self-reported voting among citizens 18 and over; state margins of error reach 5.6 points.
alt: Dots with margin of error lines for ten states’ reported turnout in 2024 against the nation’s 65.3 percent: five past the margin, five within it.
